# What the province's own name shapes cost

Corpora identical except for the pool the personas' names come from. `plain`
is the published corpus and every other number in this repository is measured
on it. `nl` swaps in the shapes that are ordinary in Newfoundland and Labrador
and were entirely absent from `plain`: apostrophes (O'Brien, O'Keefe), Mac and
Mc prefixes, accented letters, hyphenated surnames and two-token surnames
(St. Croix, Le Drew).

The remaining profiles carry one shape each, varying the surname alone with
the forenames held at the plain pool, so that a difference can be attributed
to a cause rather than only observed. Holding the forenames plain understates
each shape a little, which is the right direction for an attribution.

Nothing else differs between any two columns: same templates, same seed, same
roles, same cast sizes. Regenerate with `sever eval-names --profiles all`.

**Read the two engines with one difference in mind.** `sever` runs the
document-wide name sweep described in `results/sweep.md`, which recovers a
person's other mentions once the record has named them anywhere, and
`boundary.redact` has no equivalent. So this compares what each engine ships,
not the models underneath. The sweep accounts for most of the gap: with it
switched off `sever` scores 96.2 on `plain` and 93.4 on `nl`, within a point
of the column beside it. `results/sweep.md` is the honest place to read the
underlying detectors against each other.
